- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts peak too early and then plateau or slightly decline, while true outcomes often show sharper, delayed peaks or mean-reversion after spikes.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75), model tends to overcorrect or underestimate the subsequent decline, failing to capture volatility decay.
- Model exhibits strong upward bias in the first 10–15 days of forecast horizon, then gradually flattens — true outcomes often show more volatility and downward correction later.
- Model fails to account for mean reversion after sustained high prices; true outcomes frequently dip below forecasted levels after peak.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; true outcomes show more abrupt transitions, especially around mid-to-late horizon (days 15–30).
- Model underestimates sharp downward corrections after spikes; true outcomes often show steeper declines than forecasted.
- Model tends to ignore recent low prices in the history window, leading to persistent overestimation despite recent downward trends.
- Forecasts are not sensitive to recent volatility; true outcomes often react more strongly to short-term news or policy changes.
